focus: A12 standalone versus shared service, and env propagation to children on v2 (AI_SESSION_CHILD, OPENCODE_DB, SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE) plus service lifecycle and concurrent clients
answeredQuestions: Can one set of agent, command, skill and opencode.json files serve both versions, and where must they diverge?

label: v2 calls setup() and never server(); v1 calls server() and never setup(). A plugin exporting only one hook is a silent no-op on the other host, so a dual-host plugin must export both and route both to one bootstrap, treating the hook argument as optional.

A v2 client's env reaches server-side plugins only if that client spawned the daemon. The daemon is reparented to ppid=1 and freezes its env for life: pid 6927 saw AI_SESSION_CHILD=undefined and db=opencode-v2.db, while pid 74912 spawned by the probe client after service stop saw AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 and the client's OPENCODE_DB. AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 is therefore unreliable on v2 shared-service runs.

OPENCODE_DB is read by both versions but the on-disk formats are incompatible: v1 1.19.3 exits 1 with 'Database is not empty and has no session table' when pointed at a v2-created database, before any plugin loads. One exported OPENCODE_DB shared across hosts is a hard breakage.

v2 api --standalone does not load the project plugin tree at all: no hook fires and /api/plugin returns {data:[]}, while the identical request against the shared service loads every plugin file. Plugin loading is bound to project activation inside the service, not to the request handler.

v2 discovers all three local plugin layouts simultaneously - .opencode/plugins/*.js flat, .opencode/plugin/*.js flat, and .opencode/plugin/<name>/index.js - one setup call per file, once per project activation rather than per request (5 sequential/concurrent client calls added no hooks). Flat .opencode/plugins/*.js needs no migration on layout grounds.

v2 honours plugin (singular) in opencode.json: a file referenced only through {"plugin":["./.opencode/plugins/envprobe-alt.js"]} had its setup hook invoked. The v1 half stays open because both v1 legs died on the OPENCODE_DB incompatibility before plugin load.

Plugin process identity diverges: on v1 the plugin runs in a child of the CLI invocation (ppid=CLI pid) with that invocation's env, so in-memory plugin state is per-invocation; on v2 it runs inside the shared ppid=1 daemon, so state such as counters and locks is global across concurrent clients.

opencode2 service get returns {} and ~/.config/opencode/service.json stores only a password - no env, no database - so there is no per-invocation env contract on v2; the only levers over a child's server env are who spawns the daemon and --standalone. Recommended deep-loop dispatch on v2: run --standalone with OPENCODE_DB unset and AI_SESSION_CHILD treated as advisory.
